raw: OCTOBER 20.

translation.en: October 20

raw: We arrived here yesterday. The ambassador is indisposed, and will not go out for some days. If he were less peevish and morose, all would be well. I see but too plainly that Heaven has destined me to severe trials; but courage! a light heart may bear anything. A light heart! I smile to find such a word proceeding from my pen. A little more lightheartedness would render me the happiest being under the sun. But must I despair of my talents and faculties, whilst others of far inferior abilities parade before me with the utmost self-satisfaction? Gracious Providence, to whom I owe all my powers, why didst thou not withhold some of those blessings I possess, and substitute in their place a feeling of self-confidence and contentment?

translation.en: We arrived here yesterday.
translation.kr: 우리는 어제 이곳에 닿았네.

translation.en: The ambassador is unwell and will not go out for some days.
translation.kr: 공사는 몸이 좋지 않아 며칠은 바깥출입을 하지 않겠다고 하네.

translation.en: If he were less peevish and morose, all would be well.
translation.kr: 그가 좀 덜 까다롭고 덜 침울하기만 하면 다 좋을 텐데.

translation.en: I see only too plainly that Heaven has marked me out for severe trials; but courage — a light heart can bear anything.
translation.kr: 하늘이 나를 모진 시련에 점찍어 두었다는 것이 너무나 분명히 보이네. 그러나 기운을 내세 — 가벼운 마음이면 무엇이든 견딜 수 있으니.

translation.en: A light heart!
translation.kr: 가벼운 마음이라!

translation.en: I smile to find such a word coming from my pen.
translation.kr: 내 펜에서 그런 말이 나오다니 웃음이 나네.

translation.en: A little more lightness of heart would make me the happiest creature under the sun.
translation.kr: 마음이 조금만 더 가벼워도 나는 해 아래 가장 행복한 사람이 될 텐데.

translation.en: But must I despair of my own talents and faculties while others of far smaller ability parade in front of me in perfect self-satisfaction?
translation.kr: 그러나 나보다 한참 못한 자들이 더없이 흡족한 얼굴로 내 앞을 활보하는데, 나는 내 재주와 능력에 절망해야 한단 말인가?

translation.en: Gracious Providence, to whom I owe all my powers, why did you not withhold some of the gifts you gave me, and put in their place a feeling of self-confidence and contentment?
translation.kr: 내 모든 힘을 주신 자비로운 섭리여, 어찌하여 제게 주신 선물 가운데 얼마를 거두시고 그 자리에 자신감과 만족을 넣어 주지 않으셨나이까?

raw: But patience! all will yet be well; for I assure you, my dear friend, you were right: since I have been obliged to associate continually with other people, and observe what they do, and how they employ themselves, I have become far better satisfied with myself. For we are so constituted by nature, that we are ever prone to compare ourselves with others; and our happiness or misery depends very much on the objects and persons around us. On this account, nothing is more dangerous than solitude: there our imagination, always disposed to rise, taking a new flight on the wings of fancy, pictures to us a chain of beings of whom we seem the most inferior. All things appear greater than they really are, and all seem superior to us. This operation of the mind is quite natural: we so continually feel our own imperfections, and fancy we perceive in others the qualities we do not possess, attributing to them also all that we enjoy ourselves, that by this process we form the idea of a perfect, happy man,—a man, however, who only exists in our own imagination.

translation.en: But patience! All will yet come right; for I assure you, my dear friend, you were right.
translation.kr: 그러나 참아야지! 다 잘될 걸세. 정말이지 친구여, 자네 말이 옳았네.

translation.en: Since I have been obliged to mix constantly with other people, and to watch what they do and how they occupy themselves, I have grown far better satisfied with myself.
translation.kr: 다른 사람들과 끊임없이 섞이고 그들이 무엇을 하며 어떻게 지내는지 지켜보게 된 뒤로, 나는 나 자신에 훨씬 만족하게 되었네.

translation.en: For we are so made by nature that we are always inclined to compare ourselves with others, and our happiness or misery depends very much on the people and things around us.
translation.kr: 우리는 늘 남과 자신을 견주게끔 생겨먹었고, 우리 행복과 불행은 둘레의 사람과 사물에 크게 매여 있으니 말일세.

translation.en: For that reason nothing is more dangerous than solitude.
translation.kr: 그래서 고독만큼 위험한 것이 없네.

translation.en: There our imagination, always ready to rise, takes a new flight on the wings of fancy and paints us a whole chain of beings among whom we seem the lowest.
translation.kr: 고독 속에서 우리 상상은 언제든 날아오를 태세로 공상의 날개를 펴고, 우리가 그중 가장 못난 것처럼 보이는 존재들의 사슬을 죽 그려 내네.

translation.en: Everything appears greater than it really is, and everyone seems above us.
translation.kr: 모든 것이 실제보다 커 보이고, 누구나 우리보다 위에 있는 것처럼 보이지.

translation.en: This working of the mind is quite natural.
translation.kr: 이런 마음의 움직임은 아주 자연스러운 것일세.

translation.en: We feel our own imperfections so constantly, and fancy we see in others the qualities we lack, crediting them besides with everything we enjoy ourselves, that in this way we build up the idea of a perfect, happy man — a man who exists only in our own imagination.
translation.kr: 우리는 제 모자람을 늘 느끼고, 우리에게 없는 자질을 남에게서 본다고 여기며, 게다가 우리 자신이 누리는 것까지 그들에게 얹어 주네. 그렇게 해서 완전하고 행복한 사람이라는 관념을 지어 올리는 것이지 — 오직 우리 상상 속에만 있는 사람 말일세.

raw: But when, in spite of weakness and disappointments, we set to work in earnest, and persevere steadily, we often find, that, though obliged continually to tack, we make more way than others who have the assistance of wind and tide; and, in truth, there can be no greater satisfaction than to keep pace with others or outstrip them in the race.

translation.en: But when, in spite of weakness and disappointment, we set to work in earnest and keep steadily at it, we often find that, though we have to tack the whole way, we make more headway than others who have wind and tide to help them.
translation.kr: 그러나 약함과 실망에도 불구하고 진지하게 일에 달라붙어 꾸준히 밀고 나가면, 내내 돛을 꺾어 가며 나아가면서도 바람과 물길의 도움을 받는 이들보다 더 멀리 나아간 것을 알게 될 때가 많네.

translation.en: And in truth there is no greater satisfaction than keeping pace with others, or outstripping them in the race.
translation.kr: 그리고 사실 남들과 나란히 가거나 그들을 앞지르는 것만큼 큰 만족도 없지.

raw: November 26.

translation.en: November 26.

raw: I begin to find my situation here more tolerable, considering all circumstances. I find a great advantage in being much occupied; and the number of persons I meet, and their different pursuits, create a varied entertainment for me. I have formed the acquaintance of the Count C— and I esteem him more and more every day. He is a man of strong understanding and great discernment; but, though he sees farther than other people, he is not on that account cold in his manner, but capable of inspiring and returning the warmest affection. He appeared interested in me on one occasion, when I had to transact some business with him. He perceived, at the first word, that we understood each other, and that he could converse with me in a different tone from what he used with others. I cannot sufficiently esteem his frank and open kindness to me. It is the greatest and most genuine of pleasures to observe a great mind in sympathy with our own.

translation.en: I begin to find my situation here more bearable, all things considered.
translation.kr: 이것저것 헤아려 보면, 이곳 생활도 이제 좀 견딜 만해지기 시작하네.

translation.en: I find a great advantage in having plenty to do; and the number of people I meet, and the variety of their pursuits, make an entertaining show for me.
translation.kr: 할 일이 많다는 것이 큰 도움이 되네. 그리고 만나는 사람들의 수와 그 제각각의 일거리가 내게는 꽤 볼만한 구경거리가 되지.

translation.en: I have made the acquaintance of the Count C—, and I think more of him every day.
translation.kr: C 백작과 알게 되었는데, 날이 갈수록 그를 더 높이 보게 되네.

translation.en: He is a man of strong understanding and great discernment; and though he sees further than other people, he is not cold in his manner for all that, but capable of inspiring and returning the warmest affection.
translation.kr: 이해가 깊고 안목이 뛰어난 사람인데, 남보다 멀리 보면서도 그렇다고 사람을 대하는 태도가 차갑지 않고, 더없이 따뜻한 정을 불러일으키고 또 되돌려 줄 줄 아네.

translation.en: He seemed interested in me on one occasion when I had some business to transact with him.
translation.kr: 언젠가 그와 볼일이 있어 만났을 때 그는 나에게 관심을 보였네.

translation.en: He saw at the first word that we understood each other, and that he could speak to me in a different tone from the one he used with others.
translation.kr: 첫마디에 그는 우리가 서로 통한다는 것을, 그리고 남들에게 쓰는 것과는 다른 어조로 내게 말해도 되겠다는 것을 알아보았네.

translation.en: I cannot value his frank and open kindness to me highly enough.
translation.kr: 그가 내게 보여 준 그 솔직하고 트인 호의를 나는 아무리 귀히 여겨도 모자라네.

translation.en: It is the greatest and most genuine of pleasures to see a great mind in sympathy with our own.
translation.kr: 위대한 정신이 우리 정신과 통하는 것을 보는 것만큼 크고 참된 기쁨은 없지.

raw: DECEMBER 24.

translation.en: December 24

raw: As I anticipated, the ambassador occasions me infinite annoyance. He is the most punctilious blockhead under heaven. He does everything step by step, with the trifling minuteness of an old woman; and he is a man whom it is impossible to please, because he is never pleased with himself. I like to do business regularly and cheerfully, and, when it is finished, to leave it. But he constantly returns my papers to me, saying, "They will do," but recommending me to look over them again, as "one may always improve by using a better word or a more appropriate particle." I then lose all patience, and wish myself at the devil's. Not a conjunction, not an adverb, must be omitted: he has a deadly antipathy to all those transpositions of which I am so fond; and, if the music of our periods is not tuned to the established, official key, he cannot comprehend our meaning. It is deplorable to be connected with such a fellow.

translation.en: As I expected, the ambassador causes me endless annoyance.
translation.kr: 짐작한 대로, 공사는 내게 끝없는 짜증거리일세.

translation.en: He is the most punctilious blockhead under heaven.
translation.kr: 하늘 아래 그만큼 좀스럽게 격식을 따지는 멍청이도 없을 걸세.

translation.en: He does everything step by step, with the trifling minuteness of an old woman; and he is a man it is impossible to please, because he is never pleased with himself.
translation.kr: 노파처럼 시시콜콜 따지며 한 걸음 한 걸음 일을 처리하는데, 스스로도 만족하는 법이 없으니 남이 어떻게 해도 마음에 들게 할 수가 없네.

translation.en: I like to do business steadily and cheerfully, and when it is finished, to leave it alone.
translation.kr: 나는 일을 꾸준히 즐겁게 하고, 끝나면 손을 털고 잊는 편이 좋네.

translation.en: But he keeps sending my papers back to me, saying, "They will do" — and then recommending that I look them over again, since "one may always improve by using a better word or a more suitable particle."
translation.kr: 그런데 그는 내 서류를 자꾸 되돌려 보내며 "이만하면 되겠소" 하고는, 다시 훑어보라고 이르네. "더 나은 낱말이나 더 알맞은 조사를 쓰면 언제든 나아지는 법이니까" 하면서 말일세.

translation.en: At that I lose all patience and wish myself at the devil.
translation.kr: 그럴 때면 나는 참을성이 바닥나 차라리 악마에게나 가고 싶어지네.

translation.en: Not a conjunction, not an adverb may be left out; he has a deadly hatred of all those inversions I am so fond of; and if the music of a sentence is not tuned to the established official key, he cannot make out the meaning at all.
translation.kr: 접속사 하나 부사 하나 빠뜨려서는 안 되고, 내가 그토록 즐기는 도치법이라면 질색을 하며, 문장의 가락이 정해진 관청 어투에 맞지 않으면 뜻조차 알아듣지 못하네.

translation.en: It is deplorable to be tied to such a fellow.
translation.kr: 그런 자에게 매여 있다는 것이 한심할 노릇일세.

raw: My acquaintance with the Count C— is the only compensation for such an evil. He told me frankly, the other day, that he was much displeased with the difficulties and delays of the ambassador; that people like him are obstacles, both to themselves and to others. "But," added he, "one must submit, like a traveller who has to ascend a mountain: if the mountain was not there, the road would be both shorter and pleasanter; but there it is, and he must get over it."

translation.en: My acquaintance with the Count C— is the one compensation for such an evil.
translation.kr: C 백작과의 사귐이 이 괴로움에 대한 유일한 보상일세.

translation.en: He told me frankly the other day that he was much displeased with the ambassador's difficulties and delays, and that people like him are obstacles both to themselves and to everyone else.
translation.kr: 요전에 그는 공사의 굼뜸과 지체에 아주 언짢다고, 그런 사람은 제게도 남에게도 걸림돌이라고 솔직히 말해 주었네.

translation.en: "But," he added, "one must submit, like a traveller who has to climb a mountain: if the mountain were not there, the road would be both shorter and pleasanter; but there it is, and he must get over it."
translation.kr: "그러나" 하고 그가 덧붙였네. "산을 넘어야 하는 나그네처럼 받아들일 수밖에 없지요. 산이 없다면 길이 더 짧고 더 즐겁겠지만, 산이 거기 있으니 넘어가는 수밖에요."

raw: The old man perceives the count's partiality for me: this annoys him, and, he seizes every opportunity to depreciate the count in my hearing. I naturally defend him, and that only makes matters worse. Yesterday he made me indignant, for he also alluded to me. "The count," he said, "is a man of the world, and a good man of business: his style is good, and he writes with facility; but, like other geniuses, he has no solid learning." He looked at me with an expression that seemed to ask if I felt the blow. But it did not produce the desired effect: I despise a man who can think and act in such a manner. However, I made a stand, and answered with not a little warmth. The count, I said, was a man entitled to respect, alike for his character and his acquirements. I had never met a person whose mind was stored with more useful and extensive knowledge,—who had, in fact, mastered such an infinite variety of subjects, and who yet retained all his activity for the details of ordinary business. This was altogether beyond his comprehension; and I took my leave, lest my anger should be too highly excited by some new absurdity of his.

translation.en: The old man has noticed the count's partiality for me; it annoys him, and he seizes every chance to belittle the count in my hearing.
translation.kr: 그 늙은이는 백작이 나를 아끼는 것을 눈치챘네. 그것이 못마땅해서 기회만 있으면 내 앞에서 백작을 깎아내리려 드네.

translation.en: I naturally defend him, and that only makes matters worse.
translation.kr: 나는 당연히 백작을 감싸고, 그러면 사태는 더 나빠질 뿐이지.

translation.en: Yesterday he made me indignant, for he was aiming at me as well.
translation.kr: 어제는 나까지 겨냥하는 통에 부아가 치밀었네.

translation.en: "The count," he said, "is a man of the world and a good man of business: his style is good and he writes easily; but, like other geniuses, he has no solid learning."
translation.kr: "백작은" 하고 그가 말했네. "세상 물정에 밝고 일솜씨도 좋은 사람이오. 문장도 좋고 글도 쉽게 쓰지요. 그러나 여느 천재들이 그렇듯 탄탄한 학식은 없소."

translation.en: He looked at me with an expression that seemed to ask whether I had felt the blow.
translation.kr: 그러고는 내가 그 한 방을 느꼈는지 묻는 듯한 낯빛으로 나를 보았네.

translation.en: But it did not have the effect he wanted: I despise a man who can think and act in such a way.
translation.kr: 그러나 그가 바란 효과는 없었네. 나는 그렇게 생각하고 그렇게 행동하는 자를 경멸하니까.

translation.en: However, I made a stand and answered with not a little warmth.
translation.kr: 여하튼 나는 물러서지 않고 적잖이 열을 내어 답했네.

translation.en: The count, I said, was a man entitled to respect, both for his character and for his attainments.
translation.kr: 백작은 인품으로 보나 학식으로 보나 존경받아 마땅한 사람이라고 말일세.

translation.en: I had never met anyone whose mind was stored with more useful and wide-ranging knowledge, who had mastered such an infinite variety of subjects, and who still kept all his energy for the details of ordinary business.
translation.kr: 그만큼 쓸모 있고 폭넓은 지식을 갖춘 사람, 그토록 다양한 분야를 두루 익히고도 자잘한 일상 업무에 쏟을 기운까지 남겨 둔 사람을 나는 만난 적이 없네.

translation.en: This was entirely beyond him; and I took my leave, in case some new absurdity of his should rouse my anger too far.
translation.kr: 그에게는 아예 알아들을 수 없는 이야기였고, 나는 그의 새로운 어리석음에 화가 더 치밀기 전에 자리를 떴네.

raw: And you are to blame for all this, you who persuaded me to bend my neck to this yoke by preaching a life of activity to me. If the man who plants vegetables, and carries his corn to town on market-days, is not more usefully employed than I am, then let me work ten years longer at the galleys to which I am now chained.

translation.en: And you are to blame for all this — you, who persuaded me to bend my neck to this yoke by preaching a life of activity at me.
translation.kr: 그리고 이 모든 것은 자네 탓일세. 활동하는 삶을 살라고 설교해서 이 멍에에 내 목을 들이밀게 한 것이 자네이니.

translation.en: If the man who plants vegetables and carries his corn to town on market days is not more usefully employed than I am, then let me work another ten years at the galleys I am chained to now.
translation.kr: 채소를 심고 장날에 곡식을 마을로 나르는 사람이 나보다 더 쓸모 있게 지내는 것이 아니라면, 지금 내가 매여 있는 이 노예선에서 십 년을 더 노를 젓게 하게.

raw: Oh, the brilliant wretchedness, the weariness, that one is doomed to witness among the silly people whom we meet in society here! The ambition of rank! How they watch, how they toil, to gain precedence! What poor and contemptible passions are displayed in their utter nakedness! We have a woman here, for example, who never ceases to entertain the company with accounts of her family and her estates. Any stranger would consider her a silly being, whose head was turned by her pretensions to rank and property; but she is in reality even more ridiculous, the daughter of a mere magistrate's clerk from this neighbourhood. I cannot understand how human beings can so debase themselves.

translation.en: Oh, the brilliant wretchedness, the weariness a man is doomed to witness among the silly people one meets in society here!
translation.kr: 아, 이곳 사교계에서 만나는 시시한 자들 사이에서 보아야만 하는 그 번쩍이는 비참함, 그 지겨움이란!

translation.en: The ambition for rank!
translation.kr: 지위에 대한 욕심이라니!

translation.en: How they watch, how they toil, to gain precedence!
translation.kr: 앞자리 하나를 차지하려고 얼마나 눈치를 보고 얼마나 애를 쓰는지!

translation.en: What poor and contemptible passions they display in their utter nakedness!
translation.kr: 그 가련하고 비루한 욕심을 발가벗은 채 드러내 보이는 꼴이라니!

translation.en: We have a woman here, for instance, who never stops entertaining the company with accounts of her family and her estates.
translation.kr: 이를테면 여기 한 부인이 있는데, 제 가문과 영지 이야기로 사람들을 붙들고 늘어지기를 그치지 않네.

translation.en: Any stranger would take her for a silly creature whose head has been turned by her pretensions to rank and property; but she is in fact even more ridiculous than that — the daughter of a mere magistrate's clerk from this neighbourhood.
translation.kr: 낯선 사람이 보면 지위와 재산에 대한 허영으로 머리가 돈 어리석은 여자로 여기겠지. 그러나 실은 그보다 더 우스운데, 이 근방 한낱 서기의 딸이라네.

translation.en: I cannot understand how human beings can debase themselves so.
translation.kr: 사람이 어떻게 저렇게까지 스스로를 낮출 수 있는지 나는 이해할 수가 없네.

raw: Every day I observe more and more the folly of judging of others by ourselves; and I have so much trouble with myself, and my own heart is in such constant agitation, that I am well content to let others pursue their own course, if they only allow me the same privilege.

translation.en: Every day I see more clearly the folly of judging others by ourselves.
translation.kr: 날마다 나는 남을 제 잣대로 재는 어리석음을 더 또렷이 보게 되네.

translation.en: And I have so much trouble with myself, and my own heart is in such constant agitation, that I am quite content to let others go their own way, if they will only allow me the same.
translation.kr: 그리고 나 자신만으로도 이렇게 버거우며 내 마음이 늘 이토록 들끓으니, 남들도 제 갈 길을 가게 두는 것으로 족하네. 나에게도 그만큼만 허락해 준다면 말일세.

raw: What provokes me most is the unhappy extent to which distinctions of rank are carried. I know perfectly well how necessary are inequalities of condition, and I am sensible of the advantages I myself derive therefrom; but I would not have these institutions prove a barrier to the small chance of happiness which I may enjoy on this earth.

translation.en: What provokes me most is the wretched lengths to which distinctions of rank are carried.
translation.kr: 무엇보다 나를 분하게 하는 것은, 신분의 구별이 얼마나 한심한 데까지 밀고 나가는가 하는 것일세.

translation.en: I know perfectly well how necessary inequalities of condition are, and I am aware of the advantages I draw from them myself.
translation.kr: 처지의 불평등이 얼마나 필요한지 나도 아주 잘 알고, 내가 거기서 덕을 보고 있다는 것도 아네.

translation.en: But I would rather these institutions did not stand in the way of the small chance of happiness I might enjoy on this earth.
translation.kr: 그러나 그런 제도가 이 땅에서 내게 허락된 얼마 안 되는 행복의 기회를 가로막지는 않았으면 하네.

raw: I have lately become acquainted with a Miss B—, a very agreeable girl, who has retained her natural manners in the midst of artificial life. Our first conversation pleased us both equally; and, at taking leave, I requested permission to visit her. She consented in so obliging a manner, that I waited with impatience for the arrival of the happy moment. She is not a native of this place, but resides here with her aunt. The countenance of the old lady is not prepossessing. I paid her much attention, addressing the greater part of my conversation to her; and, in less than half an hour, I discovered what her niece subsequently acknowledged to me, that her aged aunt, having but a small fortune, and a still smaller share of understanding, enjoys no satisfaction except in the pedigree of her ancestors, no protection save in her noble birth, and no enjoyment but in looking from her castle over the heads of the humble citizens. She was, no doubt, handsome in her youth, and in her early years probably trifled away her time in rendering many a poor youth the sport of her caprice: in her riper years she has submitted to the yoke of a veteran officer, who, in return for her person and her small independence, has spent with her what we may designate her age of brass. He is dead; and she is now a widow, and deserted. She spends her iron age alone, and would not be approached, except for the loveliness of her niece.

translation.en: I have lately got to know a Miss B—, a very agreeable girl who has kept her natural manners in the middle of an artificial life.
translation.kr: 얼마 전 B 양이라는 사람을 알게 되었네. 꾸밈투성이 생활 한가운데서도 타고난 몸가짐을 잃지 않은, 아주 상냥한 아가씨일세.

translation.en: Our first conversation pleased us both equally; and when I took my leave I asked permission to visit her.
translation.kr: 첫 대화가 서로에게 똑같이 즐거웠고, 헤어질 때 나는 찾아가도 되겠느냐고 청했네.

translation.en: She agreed so obligingly that I waited impatiently for the happy moment to arrive.
translation.kr: 어찌나 선선히 응해 주던지, 나는 그 반가운 날이 오기를 조바심 내며 기다렸네.

translation.en: She is not a native of this place, but lives here with her aunt.
translation.kr: 이 고장 사람은 아니고, 숙모와 함께 여기 살고 있네.

translation.en: The old lady's face is not prepossessing.
translation.kr: 그 노부인의 얼굴은 그리 호감이 가지 않네.

translation.en: I paid her a great deal of attention, addressing most of my conversation to her; and in less than half an hour I had discovered what her niece afterwards admitted to me.
translation.kr: 나는 그 부인에게 각별히 마음을 쓰며 이야기를 거의 그쪽에 건넸고, 반 시간도 되지 않아 조카가 나중에 털어놓은 것을 이미 알아차렸네.

translation.en: Her aged aunt, having but a small fortune and a still smaller share of understanding, takes no satisfaction in anything but the pedigree of her ancestors, seeks no protection but her noble birth, and enjoys nothing but looking out from her castle over the heads of the humble townspeople.
translation.kr: 그 늙은 숙모는 재산도 얼마 없고 분별은 그보다 더 적어, 조상의 가계도 말고는 아무것에서도 만족을 얻지 못하고, 제 귀한 혈통 말고는 아무 보호도 구하지 않으며, 성에서 초라한 시민들의 머리 너머를 내려다보는 것 말고는 아무 낙도 없네.

translation.en: She was no doubt handsome in her youth, and in her early years probably trifled her time away making many a poor young man the sport of her caprice.
translation.kr: 젊어서는 틀림없이 고운 사람이었을 것이고, 한창때에는 가엾은 젊은이들을 제 변덕의 노리개로 삼으며 세월을 허투루 보냈겠지.

translation.en: In her riper years she submitted to the yoke of a veteran officer who, in return for her person and her small independence, spent with her what we may call her age of brass.
translation.kr: 나이가 든 뒤에는 늙은 장교의 멍에를 받아들였는데, 그 사람은 부인의 몸과 얼마 안 되는 재산을 받는 대가로 이른바 청동시대를 함께 보내 주었네.

translation.en: He is dead, and she is now a widow, and deserted.
translation.kr: 그는 죽었고, 부인은 이제 과부가 되어 버림받은 처지일세.

translation.en: She spends her iron age alone, and nobody would come near her, were it not for the loveliness of her niece.
translation.kr: 홀로 철의 시대를 보내고 있으며, 조카의 사랑스러움이 아니라면 아무도 가까이 가지 않을 걸세.

raw: JANUARY 8, 1772.

translation.en: January 8, 1772

raw: What beings are men, whose whole thoughts are occupied with form and ceremony, who for years together devote their mental and physical exertions to the task of advancing themselves but one step, and endeavouring to occupy a higher place at the table. Not that such persons would otherwise want employment: on the contrary, they give themselves much trouble by neglecting important business for such petty trifles. Last week a question of precedence arose at a sledging-party, and all our amusement was spoiled.

translation.en: What creatures men are, whose whole thoughts are taken up with form and ceremony, who devote years of mental and physical effort to the task of advancing themselves a single step and getting a higher place at the table.
translation.kr: 사람이란 참 묘한 존재일세. 온 생각이 격식과 예법에 붙들려 있고, 한 계단 올라서서 식탁에서 더 윗자리를 차지하려고 몸과 마음의 수고를 몇 해씩 바치니 말일세.

translation.en: Not that such people would otherwise be short of occupation — on the contrary, they make a great deal of trouble for themselves by neglecting important business for such petty trifles.
translation.kr: 그런 자들에게 달리 할 일이 없어서가 아닐세 — 오히려 그런 하찮은 것들에 매달려 중요한 일을 소홀히 하는 통에 스스로 일을 크게 만들지.

translation.en: Last week a question of precedence arose at a sledging party, and spoiled all our amusement.
translation.kr: 지난주에는 썰매 놀이에서 자리다툼이 벌어져 온 흥이 깨지고 말았네.

raw: The silly creatures cannot see that it is not place which constitutes real greatness, since the man who occupies the first place but seldom plays the principal part. How many kings are governed by their ministers—how many ministers by their secretaries? Who, in such cases, is really the chief? He, as it seems to me, who can see through the others, and possesses strength or skill enough to make their power or passions subservient to the execution of his own designs.

translation.en: The silly creatures cannot see that it is not place that makes real greatness, since the man who occupies the first place seldom plays the principal part.
translation.kr: 그 어리석은 자들은 참된 위대함을 만드는 것이 자리가 아니라는 것을 보지 못하네. 첫자리를 차지한 사람이 정작 주역을 맡는 일은 드무니 말일세.

translation.en: How many kings are governed by their ministers — how many ministers by their secretaries?
translation.kr: 얼마나 많은 왕이 제 대신들에게 휘둘리며, 얼마나 많은 대신이 제 비서들에게 휘둘리는가?

translation.en: Who, in such cases, is really the chief?
translation.kr: 그런 경우에 진짜 우두머리는 누구인가?

translation.en: The man, it seems to me, who can see through the rest, and who has strength or skill enough to make their power or their passions serve his own designs.
translation.kr: 내가 보기에는, 나머지 사람들을 꿰뚫어 보고 그들의 권세나 욕심을 제 뜻대로 부릴 힘이나 재주를 가진 사람일세.

raw: JANUARY 20.

translation.en: January 20
translation.kr: 1월 20일

raw: I must write to you from this place, my dear Charlotte, from a small room in a country inn, where I have taken shelter from a severe storm. During my whole residence in that wretched place D—, where I lived amongst strangers,—strangers, indeed, to this heart,—I never at any time felt the smallest inclination to correspond with you; but in this cottage, in this retirement, in this solitude, with the snow and hail beating against my lattice-pane, you are my first thought. The instant I entered, your figure rose up before me, and the remembrance! O my Charlotte, the sacred, tender remembrance! Gracious Heaven! restore to me the happy moment of our first acquaintance.

translation.en: I must write to you from this place, my dear Charlotte — from a small room in a country inn, where I have taken shelter from a severe storm.
translation.kr: 이곳에서 당신께 편지를 씁니다, 사랑하는 샤를로테. 모진 폭풍우를 피해 들어온 시골 여관의 작은 방에서요.

translation.en: During my whole stay in that wretched town of D—, where I lived among strangers, strangers indeed to this heart, I never once felt the least inclination to write to you.
translation.kr: 낯선 사람들 틈에서, 이 마음에는 참으로 낯선 사람들 틈에서 지낸 그 비참한 D— 마을에 머무는 내내, 당신께 편지를 쓰고 싶은 마음이 한 번도 들지 않았습니다.

translation.en: But in this cottage, in this retirement, in this solitude, with the snow and hail beating against my window, you are my first thought.
translation.kr: 그런데 이 오두막에서, 이 외진 곳에서, 이 고독 속에서, 눈과 우박이 창을 때리는 가운데 맨 먼저 떠오르는 것이 당신입니다.

translation.en: The instant I came in, your figure rose before me, and the memory of you!
translation.kr: 들어서는 순간 당신의 모습이 눈앞에 떠올랐고, 그 기억이!

translation.en: O my Charlotte, the sacred, tender memory!
translation.kr: 아, 나의 샤를로테, 그 거룩하고 애틋한 기억이!

translation.en: Gracious Heaven, give me back the happy moment when we first met.
translation.kr: 자비로우신 하늘이여, 우리가 처음 만나던 그 행복한 순간을 제게 돌려주소서.

raw: Could you but see me, my dear Charlotte, in the whirl of dissipation,—how my senses are dried up, but my heart is at no time full. I enjoy no single moment of happiness: all is vain—nothing touches me. I stand, as it were, before the raree-show: I see the little puppets move, and I ask whether it is not an optical illusion. I am amused with these puppets, or, rather, I am myself one of them: but, when I sometimes grasp my neighbour's hand, I feel that it is not natural; and I withdraw mine with a shudder. In the evening I say I will enjoy the next morning's sunrise, and yet I remain in bed: in the day I promise to ramble by moonlight; and I, nevertheless, remain at home. I know not why I rise, nor why I go to sleep.

translation.en: Could you but see me, my dear Charlotte, in this whirl of dissipation — how my senses are dried up, and my heart never once full.
translation.kr: 이 방탕한 소용돌이 속에 있는 나를 당신이 보실 수만 있다면요, 사랑하는 샤를로테 — 내 감각은 메말라 가는데 마음은 한 번도 차오르지 않습니다.

translation.en: I do not enjoy a single moment of happiness: everything is empty, nothing touches me.
translation.kr: 행복한 순간이라고는 하나도 누리지 못합니다. 모든 것이 텅 비었고, 아무것도 나를 건드리지 못합니다.

translation.en: I stand as if before a peep-show: I watch the little puppets move, and ask myself whether it is not all an optical illusion.
translation.kr: 나는 요지경 앞에 선 것 같습니다. 작은 인형들이 움직이는 것을 보며, 이것이 다 눈속임이 아닌가 자문합니다.

translation.en: I am amused by these puppets — or rather I am one of them myself; but when I sometimes take my neighbour's hand, I feel it is not a natural thing, and draw mine back with a shudder.
translation.kr: 그 인형들이 나를 즐겁게 합니다 — 아니, 나 자신이 그중 하나입니다. 그러다 이따금 옆 사람의 손을 잡아 보면 그것이 자연스럽지 않다는 것을 느끼고, 소름이 돋아 손을 거둡니다.

translation.en: In the evening I say I will enjoy tomorrow's sunrise, and yet I stay in bed; in the day I promise myself a walk by moonlight, and yet I stay at home.
translation.kr: 저녁이면 내일 해 뜨는 것을 보리라 말해 놓고도 자리에 누워 있고, 낮이면 달빛 아래 거닐리라 다짐해 놓고도 집에 머물러 있습니다.

translation.en: I do not know why I get up, nor why I go to sleep.
translation.kr: 어째서 일어나는지도, 어째서 잠자리에 드는지도 모르겠습니다.

raw: The leaven which animated my existence is gone: the charm which cheered me in the gloom of night, and aroused me from my morning slumbers, is for ever fled.

translation.en: The leaven that gave my life its rise is gone.
translation.kr: 내 삶을 부풀어 오르게 하던 누룩이 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: The charm that cheered me in the gloom of the night, and roused me out of my sleep in the morning, has fled for ever.
translation.kr: 밤의 어둠 속에서 나를 북돋우고 아침이면 잠에서 나를 깨우던 그 매력이 영영 달아났습니다.

raw: I have found but one being here to interest me, a Miss B—. She resembles you, my dear Charlotte, if any one can possibly resemble you. "Ah!" you will say, "he has learned how to pay fine compliments." And this is partly true. I have been very agreeable lately, as it was not in my power to be otherwise. I have, moreover, a deal of wit: and the ladies say that no one understands flattery better, or falsehoods you will add; since the one accomplishment invariably accompanies the other. But I must tell you of Miss B—. She has abundance of soul, which flashes from her deep blue eyes. Her rank is a torment to her, and satisfies no one desire of her heart. She would gladly retire from this whirl of fashion, and we often picture to ourselves a life of undisturbed happiness in distant scenes of rural retirement: and then we speak of you, my dear Charlotte; for she knows you, and renders homage to your merits; but her homage is not exacted, but voluntary, she loves you, and delights to hear you made the subject of conversation.

translation.en: I have found only one person here to interest me, a Miss B—.
translation.kr: 이곳에서 마음이 끌리는 사람은 단 하나, B 양뿐입니다.

translation.en: She is like you, my dear Charlotte, if anyone can possibly be like you.
translation.kr: 그이는 당신을 닮았습니다, 사랑하는 샤를로테. 누군가 당신을 닮을 수 있다면 말이지요.

translation.en: "Ah!" you will say, "he has learned how to pay fine compliments."
translation.kr: "어머!" 하고 당신은 말씀하시겠지요. "고운 말 하는 법을 배우셨군요."

translation.en: And that is partly true.
translation.kr: 그리고 그것은 얼마쯤은 사실입니다.

translation.en: I have been very agreeable lately, since it was not in my power to be otherwise.
translation.kr: 요즘 나는 아주 상냥한 사람이 되었습니다. 달리 될 도리가 없었으니까요.

translation.en: I have a good deal of wit besides; and the ladies say that nobody understands flattery better — or falsehood, you will add, since the one accomplishment always goes with the other.
translation.kr: 게다가 재담도 제법 늘었습니다. 부인들 말로는 나만큼 빈말을 잘 아는 사람이 없다더군요 — 거짓말도요, 하고 당신은 덧붙이시겠지요. 그 둘은 늘 붙어 다니니까요.

translation.en: But I must tell you about Miss B—.
translation.kr: 그러나 B 양 이야기를 해야겠습니다.

translation.en: She has an abundance of soul, which flashes out of her deep blue eyes.
translation.kr: 그이에게는 영혼이 가득해서, 그 깊은 푸른 눈에서 그것이 번득입니다.

translation.en: Her rank is a torment to her, and satisfies not one desire of her heart.
translation.kr: 제 신분이 그이에게는 괴로움일 뿐이고, 그 마음의 어떤 바람도 채워 주지 못합니다.

translation.en: She would gladly retire from this whirl of fashion, and we often picture to ourselves a life of undisturbed happiness somewhere far off in the country.
translation.kr: 이 유행의 소용돌이에서 기꺼이 물러나고 싶어 하며, 우리는 자주 저 멀리 시골 어딘가에서 누릴 방해받지 않는 행복한 삶을 함께 그려 봅니다.

translation.en: And then we speak of you, my dear Charlotte; for she knows you and pays homage to your merits — homage that is not demanded of her but freely given.
translation.kr: 그러다 당신 이야기를 합니다, 사랑하는 샤를로테. 그이는 당신을 알고 당신의 좋은 점에 경의를 표하니까요 — 누가 시켜서가 아니라 스스로 우러나서 하는 경의입니다.

translation.en: She loves you, and delights to hear you made the subject of conversation.
translation.kr: 그이는 당신을 사랑하고, 당신이 화제에 오르는 것을 기뻐합니다.

raw: Oh, that I were sitting at your feet in your favourite little room, with the dear children playing around us! If they became troublesome to you, I would tell them some appalling goblin story; and they would crowd round me with silent attention. The sun is setting in glory; his last rays are shining on the snow, which covers the face of the country: the storm is over, and I must return to my dungeon. Adieu!—Is Albert with you? and what is he to you? God forgive the question.

translation.en: Oh, that I were sitting at your feet in your favourite little room, with the dear children playing around us!
translation.kr: 아, 당신이 가장 좋아하는 그 작은 방에서 당신 발치에 앉아, 사랑스러운 아이들이 우리 둘레에서 뛰노는 것을 볼 수 있다면!

translation.en: If they became troublesome to you, I would tell them some appalling goblin story, and they would crowd round me in silent attention.
translation.kr: 아이들이 당신을 성가시게 하면 내가 무시무시한 도깨비 이야기를 들려줄 것이고, 그러면 아이들은 숨을 죽이고 내 둘레에 모여들겠지요.

translation.en: The sun is setting in glory; his last rays are shining on the snow that covers the face of the country.
translation.kr: 해가 눈부시게 지고 있습니다. 마지막 빛살이 온 들판을 덮은 눈 위에 비치고 있습니다.

translation.en: The storm is over, and I must go back to my dungeon.
translation.kr: 폭풍우는 지나갔고, 나는 내 감옥으로 돌아가야 합니다.

translation.en: Adieu! Is Albert with you? And what is he to you?
translation.kr: 안녕히! 알베르트가 당신 곁에 있습니까? 그리고 그는 당신에게 어떤 사람입니까?

translation.en: God forgive the question.
translation.kr: 이런 물음은 하느님께서 용서해 주시기를.

raw: FEBRUARY 8.

translation.en: February 8
translation.kr: 2월 8일

raw: For a week past we have had the most wretched weather: but this to me is a blessing; for, during my residence here, not a single fine day has beamed from the heavens, but has been lost to me by the intrusion of somebody. During the severity of rain, sleet, frost, and storm, I congratulate myself that it cannot be worse indoors than abroad, nor worse abroad than it is within doors; and so I become reconciled. When the sun rises bright in the morning, and promises a glorious day, I never omit to exclaim, "There, now, they have another blessing from Heaven, which they will be sure to destroy: they spoil everything,—health, fame, happiness, amusement; and they do this generally through folly, ignorance, or imbecility, and always, according to their own account, with the best intentions!" I could often beseech them, on my bended knees, to be less resolved upon their own destruction.

translation.en: For a week past we have had the most wretched weather; but for me it is a blessing.
translation.kr: 일주일째 더없이 고약한 날씨일세. 그러나 내게는 오히려 다행한 일이지.

translation.en: Since I came here, not one fine day has shone out of the heavens without being spoiled for me by somebody's intrusion.
translation.kr: 이곳에 온 뒤로 하늘에서 맑은 날이 하루라도 비치면, 반드시 누군가 끼어들어 그 하루를 망쳐 놓았으니 말일세.

translation.en: In the worst of the rain and sleet and frost and storm, I congratulate myself that it cannot be worse indoors than out, nor worse out of doors than it is within — and so I am reconciled.
translation.kr: 비와 진눈깨비와 서리와 폭풍이 한창일 때면, 집 안이 바깥보다 더 나쁠 수 없고 바깥이 집 안보다 더 나쁠 수 없으니 그만하면 됐다고 스스로를 다독이네 — 그러면 마음이 가라앉지.

translation.en: When the sun rises bright in the morning and promises a glorious day, I never fail to exclaim: "There, now, they have another blessing from Heaven, and they will be sure to destroy it."
translation.kr: 아침에 해가 밝게 떠올라 눈부신 하루를 약속할 때면, 나는 어김없이 이렇게 외치네. "자, 저들이 또 하늘에서 복을 하나 받았구나. 그리고 틀림없이 그것을 망쳐 놓겠지."

translation.en: "They spoil everything — health, fame, happiness, amusement; and generally they do it through folly, ignorance, or imbecility, and always, by their own account, with the best intentions."
translation.kr: "저들은 무엇이든 망쳐 놓네 — 건강이며 명예며 행복이며 즐거움이며. 대개는 어리석음이나 무지나 아둔함 때문이고, 언제나 제 말로는 더없이 좋은 뜻에서 그런다지."

translation.en: I could often beg them on my knees to be less determined on their own destruction.
translation.kr: 무릎을 꿇고서라도 제발 그렇게 기를 쓰고 제 발등을 찍지는 말라고 빌고 싶을 때가 많네.

raw: FEBRUARY 17.

translation.en: February 17
translation.kr: 2월 17일

raw: I fear that my ambassador and I shall not continue much longer together. He is really growing past endurance. He transacts his business in so ridiculous a manner, that I am often compelled to contradict him, and do things my own way; and then, of course, he thinks them very ill done. He complained of me lately on this account at court; and the minister gave me a reprimand,—a gentle one it is true, but still a reprimand. In consequence of this, I was about to tender my resignation, when I received a letter, to which I submitted with great respect, on account of the high, noble, and generous spirit which dictated it. He endeavoured to soothe my excessive sensibility, paid a tribute to my extreme ideas of duty, of good example, and of perseverance in business, as the fruit of my youthful ardour, an impulse which he did not seek to destroy, but only to moderate, that it might have proper play and be productive of good. So now I am at rest for another week, and no longer at variance with myself. Content and peace of mind are valuable things: I could wish, my dear friend, that these precious jewels were less transitory.

translation.en: I fear my ambassador and I shall not stay together much longer.
translation.kr: 내 공사와 나는 그리 오래 함께 가지 못할 것 같네.

translation.en: He is really growing past endurance.
translation.kr: 정말이지 더는 견딜 수 없을 지경이 되어 가네.

translation.en: He conducts his business in so ridiculous a manner that I am often compelled to contradict him and do things my own way; and then of course he thinks them very badly done.
translation.kr: 일을 어찌나 우스꽝스럽게 처리하는지, 나는 자주 그에게 반박하고 내 방식대로 할 수밖에 없네. 그러면 그는 물론 그것을 아주 잘못된 것으로 여기지.

translation.en: He complained of me lately on this account at court, and the minister gave me a reprimand — a gentle one, it is true, but still a reprimand.
translation.kr: 요전에는 그 일로 궁정에 나를 고해바쳤고, 장관은 내게 질책을 내렸네 — 부드러운 질책이기는 했네만, 그래도 질책은 질책일세.

translation.en: I was on the point of tendering my resignation when I received a letter from him, to which I submitted with great respect, on account of the high, noble, and generous spirit that dictated it.
translation.kr: 사직서를 내려던 참에 장관에게서 편지가 왔는데, 거기 담긴 높고 고결하고 너그러운 뜻에 나는 깊이 고개를 숙이고 따랐네.

translation.en: He tried to soothe my excessive sensibility, and paid a tribute to my extreme ideas of duty, of good example, and of perseverance in business, as the fruit of my youthful ardour.
translation.kr: 그는 지나치게 예민한 내 마음을 달래 주었고, 의무와 모범과 일에 대한 끈기를 두고 내가 품은 극단적인 생각을 젊은 혈기의 열매라며 좋게 보아 주었네.

translation.en: It was an impulse, he said, that he did not wish to destroy but only to moderate, so that it might have proper play and be productive of good.
translation.kr: 그것은 없애고 싶은 충동이 아니라 다만 누그러뜨리고 싶은 충동이며, 그래야 제대로 쓰여 좋은 결실을 맺으리라고 했네.

translation.en: So now I am at peace for another week, and no longer at odds with myself.
translation.kr: 그래서 나는 또 한 주 마음이 평온하고, 나 자신과도 다투지 않게 되었네.

translation.en: Contentment and peace of mind are valuable things; I could wish, my dear friend, that these precious jewels were less fleeting.
translation.kr: 만족과 마음의 평화는 값진 것일세. 친구여, 이 귀한 보석들이 좀 덜 덧없었으면 좋겠네.

raw: FEBRUARY 20.

translation.en: February 20
translation.kr: 2월 20일

raw: God bless you, my dear friends, and may he grant you that happiness which he denies to me!

translation.en: God bless you, my dear friends, and may he grant you the happiness he denies to me.
translation.kr: 하느님이 자네들을 축복하시기를, 친애하는 벗들이여. 그리고 내게는 허락하지 않으신 행복을 자네들에게는 내려 주시기를.

raw: I thank you, Albert, for having deceived me. I waited for the news that your wedding-day was fixed; and I intended on that day, with solemnity, to take down Charlotte's profile from the wall, and to bury it with some other papers I possess. You are now united, and her picture still remains here. Well, let it remain! Why should it not? I know that I am still one of your society, that I still occupy a place uninjured in Charlotte's heart, that I hold the second place therein; and I intend to keep it. Oh, I should become mad if she could forget! Albert, that thought is hell! Farewell, Albert farewell, angel of heaven farewell, Charlotte!

translation.en: I thank you, Albert, for having deceived me.
translation.kr: 나를 속여 주신 것, 알베르트, 고맙습니다.

translation.en: I waited for the news that your wedding day was fixed; and I intended on that day, with all solemnity, to take Charlotte's profile down from the wall and bury it with some other papers I have.
translation.kr: 혼례 날짜가 정해졌다는 소식을 기다리고 있었습니다. 그날이 오면 엄숙하게 샤를로테의 옆얼굴 그림을 벽에서 내려, 내가 가진 다른 종이들과 함께 묻어 버릴 작정이었지요.

translation.en: You are now united, and her picture is still hanging here.
translation.kr: 이제 두 분은 하나가 되었는데, 그 그림은 아직 여기 걸려 있습니다.

translation.en: Well, let it stay!
translation.kr: 그래, 그냥 두자!

translation.en: Why should it not?
translation.kr: 그러지 못할 까닭이 무엇인가?

translation.en: I know that I am still one of your circle, that I still hold an unspoiled place in Charlotte's heart, that I hold the second place there; and I mean to keep it.
translation.kr: 나는 아직 당신들의 울타리 안에 있고, 샤를로테의 마음속에 아직 흠 없는 자리를 지니고 있으며, 그 두 번째 자리를 차지하고 있다는 것을 압니다. 그리고 그것을 지킬 작정입니다.

translation.en: Oh, I should go mad if she could forget!
translation.kr: 아, 그 사람이 나를 잊을 수 있다면 나는 미쳐 버릴 것입니다!

translation.en: Albert, that thought is hell.
translation.kr: 알베르트, 그 생각은 지옥입니다.

translation.en: Farewell, Albert; farewell, angel of heaven; farewell, Charlotte!
translation.kr: 안녕히, 알베르트. 안녕히, 하늘의 천사여. 안녕히, 샤를로테!
